summary: Formally deprecates several IPv4 options that fell out of use but were never officially retired, which tidies up the IANA registry. It also obsoletes RFC 1385, RFC 1393, RFC 1475 and RFC 1770 and asks that they be marked Historic.

eli5.summary: Cleaning out an old toolbox: some tools nobody has used for years are officially marked as retired, so nobody wonders whether they still matter.

questions: what is the ipv4 stream id option
why were rfc 1385 and rfc 1393 made historic
subtitle: A housekeeping RFC that formally retires nine unused IPv4 header options and four old RFCs.

tldr.problem: A number of IPv4 options had become obsolete in practice but were never formally deprecated, so they still looked like live entries in the IANA registry.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6814 lists nine options, explains why each is obsolete, and has IANA mark them as deprecated in the IP option numbers registry. It also obsoletes four RFCs and asks that they be made Historic.
tldr.outcome: The registry is cleaned up and RFC 1385, RFC 1393, RFC 1475 and RFC 1770 are Historic. The document does not change the security properties of the options.

today: RFC 6814 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated. It obsoletes RFC 1385, RFC 1393, RFC 1475 and RFC 1770, which it records as Historic.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4), defined in RFC 791, lets a packet carry extra information in options placed in the variable-length IPv4 header. Each option is identified by a type value, and IANA manages the registration of those values.

Some of these options had become obsolete in practice without ever being formally deprecated. RFC 6814 deprecates them, which cleans up the IANA registry. It also obsoletes RFC 1385, RFC 1393, RFC 1475 and RFC 1770 and asks the RFC Editor to change their status to Historic.
sections.eli5: IPv4 packets can carry optional extra notes. Some of those note types are never used anymore, so this RFC officially says they are retired.

sections.title: Options Already Superseded
sections.content:
Three of the options have an obvious replacement or earlier retirement. The Stream ID option is specified in RFC 791, and the RFC calls it obsolete. It was already deprecated in Section 3.2.1.8 of RFC 1122 and Section 4.2.2.1 of RFC 1812.

The Extended Internet Protocol option is defined in RFC 1385 and is superseded by RFC 2460, the IPv6 specification. The Upstream Multicast Pkt. option was originally specified in a document called BIDIR-PIM. Its use was deprecated by RFC 5015, which uses a control-plane mechanism to solve the problem of upstream forwarding of multicast packets on a multi-access LAN.
sections.eli5: Some of the retired options were already replaced by something better, like a worn-out tool swapped for a newer one.

sections.title: Experiments That Never Spread
sections.content:
The rest were experiments or proposals that did not catch on. The RFC says that no other reference information has been found for them.

  • Traceroute is defined in RFC 1393 as Experimental. It was never widely deployed on the public Internet.
  • ENCODE was used for experimentation around IP-layer encryption. No products are known to ever have shipped with support for it.
  • VISA was part of an experiment at USC and was never widely deployed.
  • Address Extension is defined in the Experimental RFC 1475 and marked as IPv7. IPv7 was never widely deployed.
  • Selective Directed Broadcast was originally defined in RFC 1770. It was never widely deployed and the approach was abandoned.
  • Dynamic Packet State was specified in a document meant to be published as Experimental, but it never became an RFC. The option was never widely deployed.
sections.eli5: Others were science projects. People tried them, almost nobody used them, and they were quietly put on the shelf.

sections.title: The IANA Registry Changes
sections.content:
IANA keeps an "IP OPTION NUMBERS" registry listing the assigned option numbers. The registry marks a deprecated option with a footnote. RFC 6814 formally deprecates nine options, and IANA has marked them in the registry.

Each option is identified by a copy bit, a class, a number and a value. For example, Stream ID has copy 1, class 0, number 8 and value 136. Traceroute has copy 0, class 2, number 18 and value 82.

Two other options, MTU Probe (value 11) and MTU Reply (value 12), were first defined in RFC 1063. They were already deprecated by RFC 1191, so this document does not need to deprecate them.
sections.eli5: IANA keeps the official phone book of option numbers. Nine entries now carry a 'not in use' mark.

sections.title: Four RFCs Become Historic
sections.content:
Because the options they define are deprecated, RFC 6814 obsoletes four RFCs: RFC 1385 (EIP: The Extended Internet Protocol), RFC 1393 (Traceroute Using an IP Option), RFC 1475 (TP/IX: The Next Internet) and RFC 1770 (IPv4 Option for Sender Directed Multi-Destination Delivery).

The text records that, per this document, the RFC Editor has changed the status of all four to Historic.
sections.eli5: The old instruction manuals for the retired tools are moved to the museum shelf, marked Historic.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section is a single sentence: this document does not modify the security properties of the IPv4 options being deprecated. It deprecates entries in a registry and does not change how any option behaves.
sections.eli5: Putting a 'retired' sticker on a tool does not make the tool safer or more dangerous than it was.
